title: Crypto selloff broadens as Galxe pivots; portfolio falls to $67,373
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $74,400, down 2.0% over 24 hours, while ether fell 5.5% to about $2,115. Solana lost 3.7% and XRP dropped 7.0%. Selling extended across the major coins, with ether and the larger altcoins falling more sharply than bitcoin. The breadth of the decline matters: this is broader pressure on crypto prices, even though individual assets are moving at very different speeds.

Reuters reported that bitcoin and ether touched their lowest levels in more than two months during the selloff. Its report linked investor concerns to the prospect of tighter crypto oversight following Democratic victories in the US midterms, alongside continuing fallout from the Binance breach. That is a reported explanation of market sentiment. The price moves alone cannot establish how much of the decline came from politics, exchange confidence or other selling.

Galxe announced that it is consolidating its team and brand under Gravity and winding down Quest, ID and Passport. New campaigns have stopped. Existing campaign participation ends December 5, and reward claims close December 15, when the website becomes read-only. Gravity will keep operating, and Galxe says the transition does not change the G token. For projects that used Galxe to attract and reward users, this means replacing a distribution channel. For participants, the immediate practical issue is collecting outstanding campaign rewards before the deadline.

ACryptoS is winding down after an exploit that its post-mortem estimates took about $665,000 from 77 vaults across five chains. The team says a missing input check let small deposits receive excessive vault shares, diluting other depositors. Deposits have been disabled, while withdrawals remain open. The shutdown makes this more than a temporary service interruption: the team says it lacks the resources to maintain the protocol and has no plan to reopen deposits.

Our on-chain portfolio is about $67,373: $11,121 in the active treasury and $56,252 in the Safe. Its marked value is down $3,674, or 5.17%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC is worth about $46,214, nearly 69% of the total, with additional ARC exposure in the Safe’s $6,546 WETH/ARC pool. The Safe’s directly held ARC fell from 29.52 million to 27.53 million, and direct WETH fell from 2.2017 to 0.6517. The pool contains another 1.97 million ARC and 1.5421 WETH.

Beefy positions total about $2,128. Across both wallets, Aave holds roughly $7,235 of WETH collateral against $3,146 of USDC debt. Health factors have fallen from 2.33 to 2.20 in the treasury and from 1.86 to 1.76 in the Safe. Fluid remains small at about $153 net, but its $1,064 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
